cheat.summary: Working with Claude responsibly and well: the AI Fluency Framework (Description, Delegation, Diligence, Discernment), workspace features (Artifacts, Code Execution, Projects, Skills, Memory), structured prompting and iteration.

domains.title: 1. Claude Workspace & Platform Features
points: Artifacts: Use when generating procedures, templates, or one-pagers that teams need to open, edit, and maintain as a stable reference across onboarding or recurring cycles.
Code Execution: Runs code in a sandbox to perform exact calculations on multi-tab spreadsheets and generate charts; always verify computed outputs against source data before sharing.

Projects & Custom Instructions: Extract standard reference material into a Project to avoid repeating it. Specify role, instructional/brand standards, and output structure. Review periodically even if quality hasn't degraded because policies and source docs evolve.
Skills + Projects: Enable relevant Skills alongside uploaded Project knowledge sources and reference both in custom instructions.

Memory & Connectors: Memory imports from other platforms are experimental—missing details can be added manually via Settings > Capabilities. Google Drive connector summaries showing older versions usually indicate the connector's index has not refreshed yet.

domains.title: 2. The AI Fluency Framework (The 4 Ds)
points: Description: Communicate what Claude can reliably produce, known limitations, and the human oversight that remains in place—calibrated to the audience's AI familiarity.

Delegation: Driven by
  1. Need for human creativity, empathy, or judgment
  2. Task reversibility and error consequence
Never delegate final promotion decisions, employment actions without human accountability, or legally binding commitments.

Diligence: Apply organizational AI policies consistently as a sustained habit. If policy prohibits entering active HR investigation data, escalate to leadership for an approved alternative (do not use Incognito or paraphrase as a workaround). Classify mixed-sensitivity documents first before redacting PII/government IDs/payment card numbers.

Discernment: When sources conflict on a date or stat, locate the primary/authoritative source. When hallucination is suspected, first pinpoint the specific unsupported claim. Revise demographic generalizations to focus on observed customer behaviors.

domains.title: 3. Prompting, Decomposition & Iteration
points:
Prompt Structure: A strong prompt checklist requires
  1. A clear, specific task statement with required deliverable/enumerated questions
  2. Relevant context including audience and goal

Task Decomposition: Decompose when a request requires multiple distinct outputs (e.g., process map + supporting materials + measurement plan). If a 15-step output feels disjointed, consolidate related steps into fewer cohesive sections.

Iterative Refinement: First identify specific weaknesses in current output. Address specific stakeholder concerns directly while leaving approved sections unchanged. After ~8 iterations with diminishing returns, stop prompting and move to human review or a different approach.

Model Trade-offs: More capable models (Opus) handle complex extended reasoning but consume more rate limit and run more slowly; lighter models (Haiku) are faster and consume less rate limit. Alignment order: 3, 4, 1, 2, 5.

code.title: Project Custom Instructions + Skill + Brand Voice Configuration
code.description: Best-practice Project configuration that names Claude's role, enforces organizational standards/glossary, sets explicit brand voice attributes, and binds to uploaded knowledge and Skills.
code.code:
# Project Custom Instructions: Customer Support & Instructional Design

## 1. Role & Purpose
You are a Senior Course Designer and Support Specialist. Your purpose is to draft lesson outlines and customer goodwill-credit responses strictly aligned with our attached Project Knowledge Base and enabled Skills.

## 2. Brand Voice & Tone Attributes (Explicit Constraints)
- Tone: Empathetic, formal, and objective.
- Formatting: Do NOT use contractions (e.g., use "do not" instead of "don't").
- Length: Minimum 120 words; lead with the headline resolution, key drivers concisely, and forward next steps.
- Terminology: Use ONLY approved terms defined in the attached `org_glossary_v4.md`.

## 3. Policy & Grounding Rules (Preventing Hallucination)
- Rely ONLY on facts present in the supplied source documents. Do not fill perceived gaps with unverified detail.
- Recommend a goodwill credit ONLY when the attached `goodwill_eligibility_policy.pdf` explicitly permits one for the incident tier.
- Reference the active Course Design Skill for all lesson outline structures.
